why: The place-name-from-a-maps-URL rule exists TWICE and cannot be shared as code.
services/api/src/modules/ingestion/link-preview.service.ts has it in TypeScript, for a link shared
from a phone. apps/browser-extension/public/shared/link-title.js has it in plain JavaScript, for a
page saved from the desktop browser — that extension has no bundler and cannot import from a package.
Two copies of one rule is how the provider-label map ended up wrong in six places at once, with
'plaid' rendering raw on the privacy screen because one of the six was never updated. So neither copy
owns the truth: this file does, and BOTH test suites read it and fail if their implementation
disagrees. A case added here has to be satisfied on both sides or the build goes red.
Why the rule is needed at all: Google Maps serves an empty JavaScript shell to a server fetch AND
titles its own place pages 'Google Maps' in a real browser — measured in Chromium, document.title for
a Statue of Liberty place page is the literal string 'Google Maps'. So neither fetching the page nor
reading the browser's title finds the place. The URL does.

cases.note: a coordinate is not a name, and saving it records where somebody was looking
